decision: checked the review's four code citations against the source before writing any of them into the docs
why: a citation that has already moved will be copied forward and trusted
result: three of four were stale, substance of all four held

decision: scoped operation-plan.md to generated and inferred capabilities instead of writing it from scratch
why: docs/architecture.md lines 275-482 already specify the shipped plan machinery
result: avoided duplicating about 200 lines of shipped documentation

decision: kept the doc's position that activeTab alone is insufficient, against the review's correction 2
why: browser-extension.md already specified the right flow in prose; only the code block contradicted it
result: narrowed correction 2 to the WXT entrypoint block

decision: wrote scripts/check-design-docs.mjs and ran it before editing anything
why: needed a check that fails on the current docs, otherwise passing proves nothing

decision: made docs anchor code by symbol name in an HTML comment, not by line number
why: the stale citations above are exactly the drift line numbers cause

decision: split enforcement into owned and augment modes
why: the extension cannot retire a tool the page registered imperatively, so exclusive enforcement was never true there

decision: replaced single-axis trust with sourceKind, semanticProvenance, executionOwnership, contentTrust
why: native tools are authoritative about mechanics and still untrusted as content

decision: emptied matches in the runtime-registered entrypoint
why: WXT copies matches into host_permissions, so the old block requested broad access the same doc promised not to

decision: added filled, submitted, abandoned records with submitted values read from the form
why: logging the agent's input proves what was requested, not what a human sent

decision: branched milestone 1 on the registration experiment
why: forms only and bootstrap contract registered cannot both hold, bootstrap tools are imperative

decision: split risk into mutability and consequence, defaulted any mutation to CONSEQUENTIAL
why: riskBasedPolicy allows WRITE, so a POST-derived refund would have executed unapproved
result: correction 5 landed, the sharpest of the eight

decision: introduced CapabilityManifestEntry and compileManifestEntry as a compile step
why: defineCapability throws on a consequential capability with no approval evidence, so the manifest cannot feed the runtime directly

decision: replaced the rename framing with a CapabilityProvider interface extracted first
why: createAgentDeskRuntime constructs the adapter and tool surface itself, so the separation does not exist yet

decision: wrote adapter-contract.md with the adapter holding no credential and returning a request plan rather than sending it
why: approval needs the request in hand before it is sent, and an adapter that executes could bypass policy

decision: wrote operation-plan.md around PlanAssurance, computed at compile time
why: every shipped guarantee delegates to an author-supplied function that generated capabilities do not have

decision: replaced the submission-date deferral with seven checkable milestone gates
why: a date is not a safety property, and gate 2 can still change the architecture

decision: ran the check against the finished docs
why: the harness had to go from red to green on the same table

decision: rebased onto main and added the verifier prerequisite to reversal
why: PR #2 made undo depend on verify, and a generated capability usually has neither
result: anchors still resolve, four gates green
